term: aptitude for the form of another thing
definition: ForeignFormCapacity m x witnesses a possible form f of another thing and a mode in which x can have it. ForeignForm is provenance of the form, not inequality in species to x's own form. CanHaveForm is aptitude, not an actual event of acquisition or a constitutive bodily property. Cognitive is a primitive predicate for the cognitive nature under discussion; it is not defined as immateriality, intellect, or information processing.
note: Local interface for the capacity wording natum est in I q.14 a.1 co. The source reading only constrains Cognitive in one direction. The interface does not claim a sufficient account of intentionality or divine knowing; see docs/immaterial-intellect-reception.md.
